summary: Independent-review fixes for the Controller-replacement slice: a verified vm-create is a succeeded creation whatever its automatic start did (the start outcome lives in the journal start field and a failure is reported as a failed <operation>:start vm-power outcome while the VM stays a normal managed VM); an entry interrupted at the start step is settled from libvirt on report or retry, keeping a recorded reason; pending journal entries nothing in the agent process executes are reported as needs_attention outcomes; self-registered defaults carry the host's pool ID; same-key enrollment replay is bound to the token's site; outcome adoption resolves every reported outcome in one query.

guide.reason: Operator-facing semantics (a created VM whose start failed shows a failed start task and accepts power requests; orphaned interrupted requests show as needing attention) are documented by the concurrent docs record for docs/guide/*.md; this record covers the Go implementation and tests only.

api.reason: Existing contract: ManagedState.outcomes and the vm-create journal shapes are unchanged; the new <operation>:start outcome and needs_attention pending outcome use the existing ManagedOutcome fields. The reference text for these semantics is updated by the concurrent docs record for docs/API.md and docs/api/*; tests/test_api_contract passed unchanged.

state.reason: Every durable fact lives in the pool master's managed journal on Nex Core; the Controller only mirrors what the host reports.
state.record: The managed journal entry under <agent state>/managed-vms/<operation>.json: its start field records the automatic start outcome (started, or the reason) and its result/stage record the creation. A fresh Controller recovers it through ManagedEngine.Applied() in the host report (VMs plus outcomes <operation>:start and orphaned pending entries) and Controller.adoptManaged, which rebuilds the VM row and the outcome operations rows (request_id adopt-outcome:<host>:<operation>).
